# Held-out ACT rule fusion protocol

Frozen locally before computing test scores. This is a prospective analysis plan for a public benchmark, without a third-party registration or a claim that tool vendors have never seen its fixtures.

Use the W3C repository at revision 4ce3d61b6f7b04cbf2df0082a3446e97248b9124. The canonical testcase inventory defines the denominator even if every report is missing. Train on fixtures of approved rules with approved examples. Test on fixtures of proposed rules, excluding any rule ID ever designated approved in this snapshot, including IDs used in the earlier four-tool comparison. Exclude deprecated rules. Check IDs across splits, and remove test rows matching any training testcase ID or content digest (strip comments, collapse whitespace). Also audit against fixtures of the previously evaluated approved rules regardless of example approval. Record exclusions and version conflicts. Verify that report labels agree with canonical labels for matched fixtures. Study the published reports as observations. Tool vendors may know these public fixtures, and related ACT rules can share semantics.

Predict the three expected labels from only the reduced procedure outcome of each publisher-designated automated tool or linter. Reduction priority is failed, cantTell, passed, inapplicable, untested, with absence treated as untested. Never use names, URLs, rule IDs, coverage summaries, label frequencies of the test set, rule mappings, or expected labels as predictors. Use a multinomial L2 logistic stack with one-hot categorical outputs, C=1, intercept, no tuning. Give each training rule equal total weight, rescaled to mean observation weight one. Abstain for every ensemble when all its inputs are untested. Fit once and score once.

Primary measure is exact three-way label accuracy, averaged equally over held-out rules. Manual review and untested get zero credit. Compare every individual implementation report, including assisted or manual modes as contextual upper-resource comparisons. Ensembling baselines include vote over decisive labels (ties failed, passed, inapplicable), any-failure and unanimous-failure policies with plurality on the remaining labels, vote weighted by approved-rule exact accuracy, best available decisive output by training rank, smoothed confusion-matrix naive Bayes, and best subset plurality selected by macro accuracy on training, enumerating all nonempty subsets of the eligible panel. Resolve equal subset scores by smallest subset then alphabetical order. Include individual members on the same fixed inventory. Report secondary micro accuracy and failure recall plus false alerts, and shared-support sensitivity where the four original engines all give exercised outcomes. Keep the primary conclusion regardless of sensitivity results.

Compare paired rule accuracies against each comparator using a one-sided exact sign test on non-tied rules and Holm adjustment across comparisons. Publish rule win/tie/loss counts, macro differences, adjusted p values and all predictions. Count as superior only if the primary macro difference is strictly positive and adjusted p < .05 for every applicable automated tool, linter and ensemble. Include the contextual assisted/manual comparisons in adjustment for conservatism. A failed gate counts as zero additional papers. No replacement hypothesis after inspection.
